reason: Color tokens are declared once, on :root, :host in tokens/schemes.css, as light-dark(var(--femto-light-<token>), var(--femto-dark-<token>)), and --femto-box-shadow keeps a light-dark() color in each of its seven layers. getPropertyValue() returns the light-dark(...) text with the two var() references replaced by their values, alone or inside a composite value such as a box-shadow, where 2.1.1 returned the per-scheme literal. 85 tokens carry it: the 57 written with light-dark() (56 pairs and --femto-box-shadow), the tokens defined from them with var() (for example --femto-primary-hover-underline, --femto-card-box-shadow and the two --femto-group-box-shadow-focus-with-* tokens in tokens/base.css), and the generic --femto-background-color, --femto-color, --femto-border-color, --femto-box-shadow and --femto-underline that later modules set from them on elements. Without a theme file, and with each of the nine themes of tokens-dark-hover-background-contrast-style, --femto-primary-hover-background reads light-dark() of one value twice, such as light-dark(#02659a, #02659a), and --femto-primary-hover-border, which reads it, the same: femto uses one value in both schemes but keeps the pair, so that a page can set the two schemes apart. What the tokens resolve to is compared separately (kind token) and matches, except tokens-group-island-focus-ring.
notes: The 84 names a hybrid run of Styles, Color schemes and Document over every default page, all four legs, Chrome and Firefox, reported (2026-10-27), plus --femto-underline, which is probed only at anchors on links that carry data-theme (two in tokens-schemes.html). Every reported femto value contained light-dark(. The pairs moved into --femto-light-<token> and --femto-dark-<token> on 2026-11-08 without changing this text, except --femto-primary-hover-background and --femto-primary-hover-border with no theme file or one of the nine contrast-fix themes, which went from one hex value to light-dark() of it twice (the default and option presets, user-root-override's shadow-root anchors and the nine theme presets, in both schemes; in the light scheme 2.1.1's text is the hex value). static_checks.py --only fallback checks the pairs and the @supports fallback as text.

reason: 2.1.1 builds the two group focus-ring tokens on :root, :host from var(--femto-primary-focus) and var(--femto-form-element-border-color), so the value is fixed in the root's scheme and a nested data-theme island, or an element carrying data-theme itself, inherits the page's ring color. With light-dark() the token keeps the pair and resolves per element, so inside an island whose scheme differs from the page the ring takes the island's color. Only the box-shadow probe resolves these tokens.
notes: The selector matches every element that carries data-theme (article, button, details, section, span, input as well as div) and its descendants, so it reaches dialogs and cards inside islands; the root is excluded because a data-theme on html changes the root's own scheme, where both sides agree. Both values are pinned to the single-ring shape the tokens resolve to (a color, three zero offsets and a spread in px), so a missing or doubled ring, or a ring with offsets, is not registered.

reason: light-dark() follows the used color-scheme of the element it resolves on, and an author may set color-scheme on any element. In 2.1.1 such an element without data-theme switched only the browser's own colors (scrollbars, native control parts, system colors) while Pico's tokens stayed the per-scheme literals of the root's or the nearest data-theme's scheme, so the subtree mixed two schemes. In femto the tokens resolve to the author's scheme too, so text, backgrounds, borders, outlines, accent and placeholder colors switch with it. The simpler light-dark() conversion fixes the mismatch; use data-theme to theme a subtree as in 2.1.1.
notes: Fixture: div#cs-dark in tokens-schemes.html, an inline color-scheme: dark on a light page. Chrome and Firefox report only these color longhands, on the element and its ::placeholder. It is a natural-fix, like the island focus ring, the other rendered consequence of light-dark(), and not a new-token, which is for tokens that replace Sass arithmetic or a compile-time branch.

reason: Same mechanism as tokens-author-color-scheme-dark, the other way: an inline color-scheme: light on a dark page resolves femto's tokens light there, matching the browser's own light colors in that subtree, where 2.1.1 kept the page's dark literals.
notes: Fixture: div#cs-light in tokens-schemes.html. See tokens-author-color-scheme-dark.

reason: Color tokens are declared once on :root, :host and data-theme only sets color-scheme. 2.1.1 redeclared every color token on each [data-theme] element at specificity (0,1,0), which overrode an element's own lower-specificity token rules (a, button, input, select, textarea and h1 to h6 set --femto-color, --femto-background-color or --femto-box-shadow at (0,0,0) or (0,0,1)) and recomputed derived tokens such as --femto-code-kbd-color: var(--femto-background-color) from the page's colors on that element. So on a dark page <button data-theme=light> was a page-colored box while <input type=submit data-theme=light>, whose [type=submit] rule wins at (0,1,0), was a normal button. In femto an element that carries data-theme itself keeps its own color tokens in its scheme, so both are normal light buttons. The simpler conversion fixes the inconsistency. Rendered colors and box-shadows of such an element and what inherits from it change.
notes: The selector lists the elements whose 2.1.1 rules set scheme tokens on themselves at a specificity that loses to [data-theme], carrying data-theme, plus their descendants, which inherit the element's tokens (the option of a dark select differs). Narrowed to what a hybrid run of tokens-schemes.html at 1280, all four legs, Chrome and Firefox, with the three tokens-own-data-theme entries removed reported (2026-10-28): color longhands, background-color and box-shadow, in the base and focus states, only on this page. summary was dropped from the list: a summary carrying data-theme shows no difference. Fixtures: button[data-theme=dark], button.contrast[data-theme=light], input[type=submit][data-theme=dark], input[name=own-dark], input[name=own-dark-check], select[name=own-dark-select], textarea[name=own-dark-textarea], h1[data-theme=dark], a[data-theme=dark], a.secondary[data-theme=light] and span[role=button][data-theme=dark] in tokens-schemes.html.

The femto pattern leaves values containing light-dark( to tokens-light-dark-raw-text, so this entry covers only raw text that comes from the element's own rules. Narrowed to what a hybrid run of tokens-schemes.html at 1280, all four legs, Chrome and Firefox, with the three tokens-own-data-theme entries removed reported (2026-10-28): these three tokens; --femto-underline's raw text on links carrying data-theme is light-dark() text, covered by tokens-light-dark-raw-text.

reason: 2.1.1 set --femto-form-element-focus-color: var(--femto-primary-focus) on button-like inputs, checkboxes, radios and file inputs in three rules, one under each scheme selector ([data-theme=light] input, :root:not([data-theme=dark]) input, :host(:not([data-theme=dark])) input, and the two dark ones), all with the same value. Inside a shadow root whose host carries data-theme=dark, none of them match: the host is reachable only through :host(), and 2.1.1 has no :host([data-theme=dark]) rule. So those inputs kept the root value var(--femto-primary-border) and drew a solid primary ring on focus where every other checkbox and radio draws the translucent primary-focus ring. With light-dark() the per-scheme copies are identical, so femto writes one flat input:is(...) rule, which also covers these inputs (data-theme only sets color-scheme).
notes: Fixtures: the shadow-dark-host-c1 checkbox and shadow-dark-host-r radio in tokens-schemes.html, which carry data-states="focus" for this. The light host's inputs matched :host(:not([data-theme=dark])) in 2.1.1 and do not differ. :host() in Element.matches() inside a shadow tree is checked in Chrome and Firefox; Safari 27.2 reproduces it (18 records in the light-OS states pass, 12 in the dark-OS one).

reason: A user stylesheet with ':root { --femto-primary: ... }' now takes effect everywhere. In 2.1.1 it took effect only on a root carrying data-theme=dark, whose [data-theme=dark] block is (0,1,0) like the user's :root. Otherwise it lost to the light block's ':root:not([data-theme=dark])' or the media-dark block's ':root:not([data-theme])' at (0,2,0), and every [data-theme] element redeclared the tokens, undoing it inside islands. femto declares the color tokens once on ':root, :host', where :root is (0,1,0), so a later :root rule wins on the root and inherits into data-theme islands, which only switch color-scheme.
notes: Preset user-root-override loads tests/pages/assets/user-root-override.css after both sides. Every femto-side value is one of its colors, so the entry cannot register an unrelated difference. In theme-dark the differences stay inside data-theme islands, which 2.1.1 redeclared.

reason: Same cause as tokens-root-user-override-style: the raw text of the primary tokens and the tokens derived from them is the user's value at every anchor.
notes: Preset user-root-override loads tests/pages/assets/user-root-override.css after both sides. Every femto-side value is one of its colors, so the entry cannot register an unrelated difference. In theme-dark the differences stay inside data-theme islands, which 2.1.1 redeclared.

reason: femto replaces 2.1.1's per-scheme copies of --femto-form-element-focus-color: var(--femto-primary-focus) on button-like inputs, checkboxes, radios and file inputs with one flat input:is(...) rule at (0,1,1). The copies were [data-theme=light] and [data-theme=dark] input:is(...) at (0,2,1), and :root:not([data-theme=dark]), :host(:not([data-theme=dark])) and the media-dark :root:not([data-theme]) and :host(:not([data-theme])) input:is(...) at (0,3,1). A user rule loaded after femto that sets this token at specificity (0,1,1) or above, but below the matching 2.1.1 copy, now sets the control's focus ring color. The matching copy is (0,3,1) when the root does not carry data-theme=dark and (0,2,1) when it does. Examples: input[type=checkbox] at (0,1,1), [type=radio]:focus at (0,2,0). In 2.1.1 the copy outranked such a rule. Only checkboxes and radios, switches included, show it: forms/basics.css's :focus box-shadow rule is the token's only consumer on these inputs.
notes: Documentation only: no preset loads a user stylesheet that sets this token on elements, so it never hits. If one is ever added, a companion kind token entry for --femto-form-element-focus-color is needed, as for tokens-root-user-override-token. Probed with standalone pages in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160.

reason: tokens/schemes.css keeps the light and the dark value of every color token that femto or a theme gives a value per scheme, each in a token of its own, --femto-light-<token> and --femto-dark-<token> on :root, :host, and sets the token to light-dark() of the two, so it resolves as before. The theme files set these tokens too. Where light-dark() is unsupported (Chrome before 123, Firefox before 120, Safari before 17.5, Samsung Internet before 27), an @supports fallback sets each token to its --femto-light- value, so femto shows its light scheme there instead of light-dark() text that those browsers cannot use where the tokens are read. A page can set --femto-light-<token> or --femto-dark-<token> on :root to change a token in one scheme only. --femto-light-icon-valid, --femto-dark-icon-valid, --femto-light-icon-invalid and --femto-dark-icon-invalid hold the validation icons that the scheme selectors pick from. 2.1.1 has none of these names: it compiled each scheme's values into that scheme's block.
notes: 116 names: the 56 tokens tokens/schemes.css writes as light-dark(var(--femto-light-<token>), var(--femto-dark-<token>)), and icon-valid and icon-invalid. Six values are var() of another token (light form-element-placeholder-color, card-background-color and card-border-color, dark card-border-color, and both contrast-hover-underline), so they read as light-dark() text. The list follows the wrappers; static_checks.py --only fallback checks them and that every --femto-light-/--femto-dark- declaration in css/ belongs to one. Theme presets report the names too: they load css/femto.css.

reason: Contrast fix. In the dark scheme 2.1.1 gives --femto-primary-hover-background, the background of a hovered, focused or active button, [role=button] element, submit, reset or button input and file selector button, and of one with aria-current at rest, a lighter shade than --femto-primary-background, and white --femto-primary-inverse text on it falls below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast ratio in nine themes: azure #017fc0 4.38:1, blue #3c71f7 4.29:1, cyan #058686 4.41:1, fuchsia #d9269d 4.45:1, green #409614 3.76:1, jade #00895a 4.44:1, orange #e74b1a 3.88:1, pink #f42c6f 3.86:1 and zinc #6f7887 4.46:1. femto gives the token the theme's light value in both schemes, as --femto-primary-background already is: azure #02659a 6.31:1, blue #1d59d0 6.19:1, cyan #046a6a 6.41:1, fuchsia #ac1c7c 6.54:1, green #33790f 5.41:1, jade #006d46 6.41:1, orange #bd3c13 5.50:1, pink #c72259 5.52:1 and zinc #5c6370 6.05:1. --femto-primary-hover-border is var(--femto-primary-hover-background), so the border follows. The light scheme is unchanged. Every theme file sets the token as --femto-light- and --femto-dark-primary-hover-background, these nine with the light value twice, and the other 11 keep a light and a dark value: indigo, purple, red, slate and violet already give white text more than 4.5:1 in the dark scheme, and amber, grey, lime, pumpkin, sand and yellow use black text.
notes: Azure is built into tokens/schemes.css, so the default preset, the three option presets and theme-azure carry it, and css/themes/<color>.css carries it for theme-blue, -cyan, -fuchsia, -green, -jade, -orange, -pink and -zinc; the other 11 theme presets show no difference. user-root-override sets --femto-primary-hover-background on plain :root, which does not reach the kitchen sink's shadow root, so the anchors there keep azure and show the change. The 2.1.1 side is pinned to the nine dark values and the femto side to the nine light values, which keeps the entry to the dark scheme: where.schemes is not set, because the data-theme=dark islands of the light and theme-light legs show the same change. The schema cannot tie each dark value to its own theme's light value, so a swap between two of these themes would still be absorbed. Records: the background and border colors of buttons, role=button links and summaries and submit and button inputs in the dark scheme, at rest with aria-current and in the hover, focus, focus-visible and active states.
